newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sale of assets to help Mexico pay for debt support.
newsitem.headline: Sale of assets to help Mexico pay for debt support.

text.p: Mexico expects the sale of assets taken off troubled banks will help cut the cost of its debtor bail-out programs next year, Finance Ministry spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela said on Wednesday.

"When we start up the Valuation and Sale of Assets Program, that will possibly begin in the first quarter of 1997, that also is going to help cut the cost (of debt support programs)," Valenzuela told a news conference.

The VVA, as the sale of assets program is known in Spanish, will seek to put on the market foreclosed properties and other assets given to the Bank Insurance Fund, Fobaproa, by banks in exchange for capital to help them weather the problem of unpaid debts.
The Mexican government says the cost of its debt support programs runs to about 210 billion pesos, or 8.4 percent of GDP.

But he said a budget surplus, spare funds from Banco de Mexico and some 15.1 billion of loans from the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank had enabled the government to deal with about 55 billion pesos worth, leaving the equivalent of 6.2 percent of GDP left to pay off.
